title: Case report: DSP truncation variant p. R1951X leads to arrhythmogenic left ventricular cardiomyopathy
case_prompt:
A 21-year-old university student experienced syncope shortly after exercise. He reported no chest pain or dyspnea but had a self-limited diarrheal illness two weeks earlier. In the emergency department he was afebrile, blood pressure was 127/78 mmHg, heart rate 81 beats/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. Examination was unremarkable. His mother had idiopathic cardiomyopathy; his maternal grandmother died of sudden cardiac arrest.

On telemetry, he developed sustained monomorphic ventricular tachycardia with a cycle length of 220 ms, treated with intravenous metoprolol, amiodarone, and lidocaine. In the coronary care unit, he had polymorphic VT that degenerated into ventricular fibrillation; he was successfully defibrillated.

Serum chemistry was normal. Initial troponin I was 0.23 ng/mL (normal <0.04 ng/mL) and subsequently decreased. Pre-arrest ECG showed sinus rhythm with premature ventricular complexes of left bundle branch block, inferior axis morphology; there were no epsilon waves, precordial T-wave inversions, conduction delays, or QT prolongation. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a dilated left ventricle with ejection fraction 45% and severe basal-anterior hypokinesis with mild hypokinesis of adjacent segments. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated sub-epicardial late gadolinium enhancement in the basal-anterior and basal anterolateral segments and additional mid-inferior and mid-anteroseptal enhancement. The right ventricle was normal in size and function without late enhancement. An endomyocardial biopsy showed mild lymphocytic myocarditis, interstitial fibrosis, and myocyte hypertrophy.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Giant cell myocarditis was considered — “An endomyocardial biopsy was performed to rule out giant cell myocarditis.”
2. Viral myocarditis was considered — “Biopsy demonstrated mild lymphocytic myocarditis, interstitial fibrosis, and myocyte hypertrophy.”
3. Sarcoidosis was considered — “Ventricular arrhythmias and fibrosis in ALVC can be misattributed to viral myocarditis or sarcoidosis.”
4. Arrhythmogenic left ventricular cardiomyopathy was considered — “CMR imaging showed sub-epicardial basal-anterior and basal anterolateral late gadolinium enhancement… The right ventricle was of normal size and function and without LGE.”
